data.name: Muthlaq
data.gender_notes: Muthlaq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'th-l-q', meaning 'to purify, to sanctify, to cleanse'. In Islamic context, Muthlaq refers to someone who has been purified through spiritual and moral growth. It is a name of reverence and respect, often given to those who have shown remarkable devotion and commitment to their faith. The name Muthlaq carries the meaning “Purified, sanctified” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muthlaq usually hope their child will grow to embody purified, sanctified and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who strive for spiritual perfection and seek to purify their souls
data.etymology: Muthlaq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Purified, sanctified.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muthlaq total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_english.name: Muthlaq
in_english.meaning: Prideful, miserly, unwilling to accept other's words, wasteful with money, unwilling to earn money, fearful of losing money
in_english.long_meaning: Muthlaq: A person who is prideful, miserly, unwilling to accept other's words, wasteful with money, unwilling to earn money, fearful of losing money, and who considers his own wealth to be the only wealth. He is a person who is always worried about losing his wealth, and who is never willing to accept any advice or guidance from others. He is a person who is always looking for ways to increase his wealth, but who is never willing to take any risks or make any sacrifices. He is a person who is always complaining about the lack of wealth, and who is never satisfied with what he has. In Islamic tradition, Muthlaq is considered to be a person who is prone to pride and arrogance, and who is unwilling to accept any guidance or advice from others.
